a4.speaker: Maria Barron, USAID Niger Mission Director
a4.speech: Support from the Hamzari program enabled more than 17,000 farmers to learn and apply improved production techniques, allowing them to increase their agricultural production ; the project also enabled more than 58,000 people to have better access to drinking water, improving their quality of life and reducing the risk of water-related diseases ; in total, the Hamzari project directly benefited more than 104,000 people, 62% of whom were women, reaching 106% of its initial target.

a307.speaker: Isaac Muchokomori, acting postmaster general, Zimpost
a307.speech: Speaking during the launch at Greendale Post Office in Harare, said the new mobile money platform will... [text truncated]

a330.speaker: Dr Peter Koll, Johannesburg gynaecologist
a330.speech: “About 10 years of life is lost,” referring to the earlier onset of cervical cancer among HIV-positive women.

a330.speaker: Dr Peter Koll, Johannesburg gynaecologist
a330.speech: “There is no theoretical reason for it to be unsafe (in HIV-positive women),” argues Koll, and says that one should balance the risk of cervical cancer against an improbable negative effect from the vaccine.

a330.speaker: Nomfundo Eland, national women’s rights campaign manager of the Treatment Action Campaign (TAC)
a330.speech: “HPV-infection rates among HIV-positive women are ten times greater than those among HIV-negative women” ; “This is partly due to the compromised immunity of HIV-positive women.”

a330.speaker: Nomfundo Eland, national women’s rights campaign manager of the Treatment Action Campaign (TAC)
a330.speech: “Roughly 80% of these cases (cervical cancer) are in the developing world” ; “Generally due to poor screening programmes and diagnostics in these communities.”

a330.speaker: Some experts (unnamed)
a330.speech: Estimate that up to 80% of sexually active adults are infected with HPV.

a330.speaker: Professor Lynette Denny, University of Cape Town
a330.speech: “Because HPV-associated disease is so prevalent in HIV-positive women, it would be particularly useful to vaccinate women who might become HIV positive in the future, so that they are protected,” she told Mail & Guardian Online.

a330.speaker: David Pritchard, general manager of GlaxoSmithKline (GSK)
a330.speech: “We don’t claim that it is effective in HIV-positive people.”

a330.speaker: Cancer Association of South Africa (CANSA) and the Treatment Action Campaign (TAC)
a330.speech: Have called on the SA government to implement the vaccine into the public health system, as countries such as the USA, UK and Australia have done.

a330.speaker: GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) and MSD
a330.speech: Both have expressed a willingness to negotiate with government on a lowered price for public roll-out.

a461.speaker: Titus Maluleke, Governor of Masvingo province, Zimbabwe
a461.speech: “These organisations have left us with no choice except to suspend them from operating in the province with immediate effect as they have twice failed to submit to the requirements of our laws,” said Titus Maluleke, the governor in question, to the state-run Herald newspaper.

a461.speaker: Titus Maluleke, Governor of Masvingo province, Zimbabwe
a461.speech: Elaborated on his reasons for banning the affected NGOs: “Some NGOs sneak into the provinces undercover and we only discover that there is something happening when there is a gathering where people are being registered for, we are told, humanitarian aid,” he said. “Yet there are clandestine, high-profile visits from overseas to the villages, bypassing all other levels. That should be stopped and that is what we are trying to end.”

a461.speaker: Zanu-PF party report (as reported by New Zimbabwe)
a461.speech: A party report said there were around 2,500 NGOs in Zimbabwe, and that not all of them were friendly. “Some of these NGOs are working day and night to remove President Mugabe and Zanu-PF from power. They are being funded by Britain and some European Union countries, the United States, Australia, Canada and New Zealand,” said the report.

a461.speaker: The Herald (state-run newspaper, column)
a461.speech: Described NGOs as “civil society mercenaries” in a scathing column.

a461.speaker: Egyptian state media
a461.speech: On Tuesday, state media in Egypt ran front-page headlines accusing America of spreading “anarchy” in Egypt through its NGO funding.

a461.speaker: Reuters
a461.speech: Described that banning foreign NGOs made it “difficult for the outside world to provide humanitarian assistance or monitor a vote marred by political violence and voter intimidation”.

a479.speaker: UHURU Tech Solution, Liberian ICT group
a479.speech: Has called on the government of Liberia to invest in cyber security education and robust legislation to address cyber-crimes in Liberia.

a479.speaker: Foldestine Paye, Chief Executive Officer of UHURU Tech Solution
a479.speech: Called on the Liberian government to invest in cyber security education to ensure both the youth and adults are equipped with knowledge to navigate the digital landscape safely; added that the government should establish partnership with educational institutions, technology companies, and international organizations to help develop an effective training program to foster a safe internet environment; stressed the importance of fostering a culture of cyber security awareness among students to create a safer online environment.

a479.speaker: Foldestine Paye, Chief Executive Officer of UHURU Tech Solution
a479.speech: "We are calling on the government to pass the cyber security law which in the Telecommunication room, and a robust legislation to address cyber security crimes. We also want to use this medium to call on the Liberia Telecommunication Authority (LTA) to create the Cyber Security Regulatory Framework to protect the people of Liberia in the cyber space" ; called on the LTA to set up a Digital Forensic Lab (DFL) and the Cyber Response Unit (CRU) to protect people in the cyber world; said establishing these clear policies will not only detect potential threats, but also provide a framework for accountability in committing cyber crimes ; "We need robust legislation to combat cybercrimes" ; stressed that collaboration between public and private sectors is crucial for developing comprehensive strategies to combat cyber threats.

a479.speaker: Foldestine Paye, Chief Executive Officer of UHURU Tech Solution
a479.speech: Acknowledged the youth as leaders of tomorrow, noting their profound engagement with technology; stressed that cyber threats are real, stating that from identity theft and cyber bullying to scams and misinformation, the dangers are numerous; emphasized the importance of people educating themselves about these risks and knowing how to protect personal information; urged internet users to use strong, unique passwords, think before sharing, and always question the validity of online sources, cautioning that once information is shared online, it can be challenging to retract.

a479.speaker: Florence Gaye, DMG HR
a479.speech: Noted that the symposium is held in commemoration of Cyber Security Month, celebrated each October, a global initiative that aims to educate individuals and raise awareness about the importance of cyber security.

a479.speaker: Cllr. T. Emmanuel Tomah, representing the Liberia Telecommunications Authority (LTA)
a479.speech: Recounted that in 2011 the Economic Community of West African States at its Extraordinary Sitting in Abuja, Nigeria adopted nine supplementary acts, three of which were data protection, electronic transaction, and the cybercrime act, which Liberia is signatory to; said the supplementary acts cover thematic areas including fraudulent access to computer systems, fraudulent data remaining in the computer, interference with operations of a computer system and fraudulent interception of computer data, and have since served as a guide for Liberia's cyber space; informed the occasion that Liberia has, in line with international protocols and treaties, adapted a supplementary act as a framework for the governance of cyberspace so that the country's cyber security policies are aligned with global standards and best practices.

a479.speaker: Cllr. T. Emmanuel Tomah, representing the Liberia Telecommunications Authority (LTA)
a479.speech: Said the LTA is partnering with the National Identification Registry (NIR) on SIM card registration to better track cyber activities in the country, a collaboration aimed at enhancing accountability and security in the telecommunications sector; encouraged participants to be good citizens as they navigate the internet, reminding them of their responsibility in fostering a safe online community.

a626.speaker: Authorities in the Abyei Administrative Area
a626.speech: Report that 24 people have died and over 1,000 others have been admitted with cholera in recent days, as the region struggles with a severe outbreak without access to vaccines.

a626.speaker: Yohana Akol, Minister of Information in Abyei
a626.speech: Confirmed to Eye Radio that the area has recorded 24 deaths and 1,054 cholera cases in just two weeks, warned that the cholera situation is worsening daily and that health facilities are overwhelmed by the surge in patients, lacking crucial vaccines, and stated that the hardest-hit area is Amiet Market, which hosts a large population of returnees and refugees from Sudan: “The cholera situation is continuously worsening and at a very high level. There are now 1,054 recorded cases of cholera” ; “The area with the highest number of cases is Amiet Market, northeast of Abyei. It is a densely populated market, including refugees fleeing the civil war in Sudan, stranded returnees who have settled in Abyei, and the host population. The death toll, according to the latest updates from the Ministry of Health, has now reached 24 due to the cholera outbreak in the area.”

a626.speaker: Yohana Akol, Minister of Information in Abyei
a626.speech: Appealed to the National Ministry of Health to urgently dispatch cholera vaccines to the area: “We appeal to the National Ministry of Health, especially the Minister, Hon. Sarah Clito, to fulfil her promise to intervene with the vaccination as an immediate response” ; “Until now, the vaccination has not reached the area. Therefore, we appeal to the national government to expedite the vaccination process, as the health situation is deteriorating and timely support is needed to save lives.”

a626.speaker: Ministry of Health (latest updates, cited)
a626.speech: Latest updates put the death toll from the cholera outbreak in the area at 24.

a701.speaker: Colonel Assa Badiallo Touré, Malian Minister of Health and Social Development
a701.speech: Hailed "the efforts of humanitarian action in 2024, which made it possible to save lives and ease the suffering of more than 1.8 million people." ; Urged "Mali's partners to continue this momentum in the interest of the Malian people and with respect for national sovereignty." ; Stressed that despite these efforts, "about 6.4 million people, or 27.7% of the current population, need humanitarian aid and protection." ; "The Mali 2025 humanitarian response plan targets 4.7 million of them, among the most vulnerable, needing assistance in priority sectors such as protection, education, food security, health, nutrition, shelter and essential household items, as well as water, hygiene and sanitation, for an amount of $771.2 million."

a701.speaker: Khassim Diagne, interim Humanitarian Coordinator for Mali
a701.speech: Expressed his thanks "to the Malian authorities for their commitment and unfailing support for the humanitarian mandate, and to the humanitarian partners for their dedication and their work in the service of the most vulnerable populations, often at the risk of their own safety."

a706.speaker: An AFP photographer (eyewitness account)
a706.speech: According to the explanations of an AFP photographer, one of the devices tore off a rescue worker's hand when it exploded.

a744.speaker: Oketsang (police spokesperson, Botswana)
a744.speech: Stated that following the collision, the GD6 caught fire along with the trailer it was pulling, which carried huge luggage that burnt to ashes; said the Toyota GD6 bearing South African plate numbers was driven by a 23-year-old Zimbabwean man and it was heading to the north coming from the south ; "The Toyota Camry that was driven by a 60-year-old Motswana man was facing south from the northern part of the country when the vehicles collided. The GD6 had three people on board, the driver and two male passengers who are all currently fighting for their lives at Nyangabgwe Referral Hospital {in Francistown} together with the sole survivor of the Toyota Camry."

a911.speaker: Mutaz Musa, Prime Minister of the Republic of Sudan
a911.speech: In his opening address, stressed that the East African region was making progress in building bridges and democracy in its quest for lasting peace, security and stability: “These efforts will not only create a more favourable environment for the advancement of its citizens, but will also guarantee the realisation of their long-held dream of development and well-being.”

a911.speaker: Mutaz Musa, Prime Minister of the Republic of Sudan
a911.speech: Congratulated the EASF on its efforts in recent years to establish a regional force and maintain its operational readiness, telling the member states’ defence ministers: “The EASF needs all the necessary support to strengthen its capacities in different areas. During this meeting, I believe you will contribute enormously to identifying some of the critical areas in which the EASF needs more support.”

a911.speaker: Mr Rwamirama, Minister of State for Defence and Veteran Affairs of Uganda and Chairman of the EASF Council of Ministers
a911.speech: Spoke of the historic character of relations between EASF member states, which share many common interests, values and objectives: “The essential roles that the countries play on the regional and continental stage advance the cause of African unity in building the desired future.”

a911.speaker: Abdillahi Omar Bouh, Director of the EASF
a911.speech: Indicated that “four years after reaching its full operational capability (FOC), the EASF was continuing to strengthen its forces and was focusing more on conflict prevention through the continuous improvement of organisational early-warning systems. This will include developing the panel of the wise for its involvement in mediation and negotiation. In addition, the EASF plans to create a maritime coordination centre (MCC), which is in its initial formation phase.”

a911.speaker: Abdillahi Omar Bouh, Director of the EASF
a911.speech: Expressed his gratitude to the African Union Commission (AUC), the Friends of the EASF and partners for the technical, logistical and financial support given to the EASF Secretariat in planning and implementing its activities over the years.

a1027.speaker: Xi Jinping, Chinese President
a1027.speech: Opened the eighth Forum of China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) in Dakar by pledging another billion doses of COVID-19 vaccines and more private-sector equity investment to Africa.

a1027.speaker: Voices from the Global South
a1027.speech: Have increasingly lamented that evaluations of debt sustainability - such as the joint International Monetary Fund-World Bank Debt Sustainability Analysis Framework - have tended to focus narrowly on liabilities, without taking adequate account of the asset side of the public-sector balance sheet.

a1027.speaker: World Bank, Changing Wealth of Nations 2021 report
a1027.speech: Cited as going some way toward filling the knowledge gap on the value of public-sector assets and net worth, making it an invaluable resource for policymakers today.

a1027.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister (2020 FOCAC speech)
a1027.speech: Noted that China financed, constructed, and completed thousands of hard and soft infrastructure projects in Africa in the first two decades of this century, including over 6,000km of railways, roads covering roughly the same distance, nearly 20 ports, over 80 large-scale power plants, more than 130 medical facilities, 45 stadiums, and 170 schools.

a1027.speaker: Study by the authors (Justin Yifu Lin and Yan Wang)
a1027.speech: According to their study, some 75-78pc of China-financed projects completed in 54 African countries between 2000 and 2014 addressed one of five key bottlenecks; targeting problems afflicted 22pc of completed hard-infrastructure projects and 26pc of soft-infrastructure projects, meaning they were not genuinely demand-driven.

a1027.speaker: Research by the Boston University Global Development Policy Center
a1027.speech: Has revealed concerns about the social and environmental effects of these projects.

a1027.speaker: China (government commitment)
a1027.speech: Has committed to stop financing coal-fired power plants and to invest more in renewables.

a1027.speaker: Updated Chinese aid data
a1027.speech: According to the data, over 60pc of Chinese investment projects are in green sectors.

a1102.speaker: Paul Kagame, President of Rwanda
a1102.speech: At the EAC-SADC summit in Dar es Salaam on 8 February 2025, rejected the DRC's accusations and attributed the escalation of tensions to Kinshasa, calling for concrete actions to resolve the security crisis in eastern DRC; rejected any responsibility of Rwanda in the accusations formulated by the DRC and denounced a deliberate strategy by Kinshasa seeking to implicate Kigali in a conflict that he considers does not concern his country.

a1102.speaker: Paul Kagame, President of Rwanda
a1102.speech: Expressed his displeasure at the Congolese accusations, stating that it was unacceptable for the DRC to try to silence Rwanda while it was fuelling a security crisis against it ; "No one can tell us to shut up," he hammered, underlining that Rwanda had made repeated calls for dialogue without any response from the Congolese authorities ; "We have been begging the DRC and its leaders for a long time. We have shared our problems and asked the DRC to address them, and they have refused."

a1102.speaker: Paul Kagame, President of Rwanda
a1102.speech: Insisted that the current crisis in the DRC was deeply rooted in old ethnic tensions, exacerbated by policies of marginalisation; warned that this situation could have serious repercussions at the regional level and underlined that Rwanda could not remain passive in the face of this development ; "What is happening there is an ethnic war that has been in preparation for a long time, denying people's rights and then attacking Rwanda. You must recognise people's rights and take a step to solve the problem." ; "This war was triggered by the DRC and not by Rwanda. It was imposed on us and we were asked to bear it. We cannot accept it."

a1102.speaker: Paul Kagame, President of Rwanda
a1102.speech: Warned against the ineffectiveness of diplomatic meetings that do not lead to concrete actions and urged participants not to settle for sterile discussions but to work actively for lasting solutions ; "Let us not settle for another meeting like the one we have had. Let us use this meeting in a way that takes all these questions seriously into account and let us find a lasting solution," he concluded.

a1102.speaker: EAC-SADC joint summit of heads of State (resolutions)
a1102.speech: Adopted several resolutions aimed at restoring stability in eastern DRC: the heads of State present demanded an immediate ceasefire, the reopening of Goma airport and the resumption of negotiations with all parties, including the M23 rebel group; a meeting of the EAC and SADC chiefs of defence forces is planned within five days to develop strategies for securing the region and facilitating humanitarian aid; the summit also insisted on the need to neutralise the FDLR and to establish a plan for the withdrawal of uninvited foreign armed forces from Congolese territory.

a1209.speaker: Bayt Mal Al-Quds agency (video and photos published)
a1209.speech: A video released on Monday by the Bayt Mal Al-Quds agency shows trucks loaded with supplies travelling through the streets of Gaza. The trucks bore the Moroccan flag and the logo of the Mohammed V Foundation for Solidarity. The agency then published photos showing Moroccan food aid, including baby food, canned goods, flour and fruit, reaching storage centres in Deir el-Balah, a city in central Gaza.

a1209.speaker: Many Palestinians
a1209.speech: This aid was welcomed by many Palestinians, who say it helps meet urgent needs.

a1209.speaker: Humanitarian organisations
a1209.speech: warn that the volume of aid is still far from sufficient.

a1209.speaker: Gaza government press service
a1209.speech: indicated that only 85 trucks of humanitarian aid had entered the enclave yesterday, and that many of them had been looted before reaching people in need. The press service and the United Nations both indicated that between 500 and 600 trucks were needed each day to provide adequate aid to the population, reduce looting and bring down the high prices caused by shortages.

a1209.speaker: United Nations
a1209.speech: indicated that between 500 and 600 trucks were needed each day to bring adequate aid to the population, reduce looting and lower the high prices caused by shortages.

a1209.speaker: Gaza Ministry of Health
a1209.speech: According to the Gaza Ministry of Health, at least 135 Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks over the last 24 hours, including 87 people who were waiting for aid. These attacks also left 771 wounded. The ministry indicated that five people died of hunger during the same period, bringing the total number of hunger-related deaths to 193, including 96 children.

a1492.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a1492.speech: Told journalists, regarding President Trump’s early departure from the G7 leaders’ summit: “President Trump cut the meeting short and returned to America in order to persuade Israel and Iran to agree to a ceasefire…”

a1492.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a1492.speech: Dismissed his French counterpart’s remarks: “President Macron is mistaken because he does not understand the reason for my return. I am returning to America because we want something much bigger than a ceasefire…” ; At a time when the conflict between the two countries is entering a dangerous phase, Trump said a ceasefire was not necessary, said Iran must not be allowed to possess nuclear weapons, and warned the residents of Tehran to leave their homes immediately.

a1664.speaker: Apostle Clifford Kawinga, Salvation for All Ministries
a1664.speech: Stated that the outreach also marks the official opening of a new branch of the church, further expanding the ministry's efforts to spread the gospel and serve the community. "We believe that through our new branch, we will support many souls through spiritual encouragement and humanitarian aid."

a1664.speaker: Charles Kanjoka, representative of Senior Chief Makuwira
a1664.speech: Expressed gratitude for Kawinga's encouragement in their spiritual lives. Noted that the donation is timely, as the area has been severely impacted by several recent cyclones. He encouraged Kawinga and his team to continue their efforts to reach out to those in need with both spiritual and humanitarian assistance.

a1855.speaker: Zumunta Association USA Inc. (Nigerian diaspora group)
a1855.speech: Said on Monday that it will train 1000 youths in ICT and Artificial Intelligence (AI) during its 2025 Annual Convention.

a1855.speaker: Sunday Bitrus, National President of Zumunta Association USA Inc.
a1855.speech: Disclosed that the convention, which is the association's second in Nigeria in its 35 years of existence, will hold in Nasarawa State ; said the 2025 Zumunta Convention will feature a robust lineup of other high-impact programmes, which include a free medical outreach, golf and tennis tournaments, strategic business meetings on key sectors including agriculture, mining, health, and housing, as well as participation in the National Diaspora Day and Diaspora Week activities in Abuja ; said the convention, themed "From Connection to Action: Mobilizing Local Experience and Diasporan Insights for National Development," will run from July 14-23, 2025, aligning with the National Diaspora Day and Diaspora Week celebrations in Abuja slated for July 25-26, 2025, and that the Convention focus on impactful engagement and collaborative action.

a1855.speaker: Sunday Bitrus, National President of Zumunta Association USA Inc.
a1855.speech: Recalled that Zumunta's scholarship scheme has empowered over 5,000 science students in Northern Nigeria, with N100 million disbursed to date, and added that the Association has also implemented health and palliative projects in partnership with over 30 Non-Governmental Organisations ; "We are shifting from connection to action, from diaspora dialogues to real-time delivery at home."

a1855.speaker: Abike Dabiri-Erewa, Chairman/CEO Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NIDCOM), represented by Dr. Sule Yakubu Bassi, Secretary to the Commission
a1855.speech: Described the return of the Zumunta Convention as a milestone in diaspora engagement: "Zumunta is demonstrating that the diaspora is not just watching, they are working. This 2025 convention showcases the power of collaboration between diaspora organisations, state governments, and federal institutions. NIDCOM is proud to support this initiative that aligns with our mandate to promote structured, impactful diaspora contributions to national development."

a1880.speaker: Edwina Kolleh, Coordinator of the Liberian Students Union in China’s Hunan Province
a1880.speech: highlighted various areas the Liberian Government can leverage to put the country on par with its counterparts across the globe, naming security, education, tourism, and infrastructure development as crucial areas for possible urgent improvement: “These sectors are not only vital to the growth of the country, but are also critical to elevating the living standards of the citizens”.

a1880.speaker: Edwina Kolleh, Coordinator of the Liberian Students Union in China’s Hunan Province
a1880.speech: wants the government to pay keen attention to the promotion of the preservation of the country’s cultural values and norms, ensuring that the sector becomes a part of the governance process; she also placed emphasis on the construction of more roads to boost trade and enhance mobility among citizens across the country.

a1880.speaker: Varney Johnson, former President of the Liberian Students in Hunan Province
a1880.speech: is urging the Liberian government to further invest more in its Education Sector, especially in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM): “The provision of modern research equipment, coupled with the construction of conducive educational facilities across the country, will further improve Liberia’s Education Sector.” He also highlighted the revision of the academic curriculum to include areas of research activities to broaden the minds of students in the country.

a1880.speaker: Varney Johnson, former President of the Liberian Students in Hunan Province
a1880.speech: stressed the need for the Civil Service Agency (CSA) to be revamped, ensuring that jobs are given to citizens based on qualification, not on personal interest, noting that such a move will put Liberia on par with countries like China, the U.S, and Japan, and saying that the interests of Liberians should be put at the forefront at all times.

a1896.speaker: Mohamed Houmed Abass, Prefect of Tadjourah
a1896.speech: Expressed his enthusiasm for this government initiative. He affirmed his willingness to support the project's actors at every stage of its implementation.

a1896.speaker: Baragoïta Saïd, agronomist and chief Coordinator of the Support Project for Resilient Agricultural Value Chains (FAR)
a1896.speech: Informed the region's farmers that he was taking part in this workshop with immense pleasure. He underlined the new policy direction in agricultural development, aimed at improving competitiveness and responding to the needs of the local market.

a1896.speaker: National consultant, facilitator of the workshop (unnamed)
a1896.speech: Explained the components of the project, in particular those linked to basic infrastructure, support for farmers in accessing financing, and the development of agricultural value chains ; set out to participants the ins and outs of the paradigm shift for the development of the country's rural areas: the new paradigm follows a twin track which consists firstly of promoting entrepreneurship and bankable private sector investments in connection with financial partners for commercial and profitable agriculture, and secondly of supporting regional hubs with development potential where basic services and infrastructure will be concentrated.

a2108.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2108.speech: Has decisively announced a 36 percent reduction in borrowing costs, which took effect on November 1 2024, translating into annual savings of $1.2 billion for developing nations, enhancing their financial capacity to "effectively tackle pressing economic challenges".

a2108.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva, IMF Managing Director
a2108.speech: Stated at a press conference last week that the landmark decision had received unanimous backing from member states at their annual meeting in Washington, D.C.: "For the first time ever, we have lowered borrowing charges for lenders, resulting in annual savings of $1.2 billion" ; explained that the pivotal decision was rooted in a comprehensive three-pillar approach designed to drive economic growth, mobilize domestic revenues, and secure adequate financing through international financial institutions, while facilitating private sector investments at reduced costs.

a2108.speaker: Mahomed Aljadaan, IMF Chairperson
a2108.speech: Asserted that these reforms were specifically crafted to ensure that low-income countries transitioned from a trajectory of low growth and high debt: "We are committed to fostering self-lending while refining our strategies to mitigate high debt situations among low-income nations." ; highlighted the IMF's determined efforts to enhance capacity development assistance and secure necessary financing for these countries, and underscored the urgent need to improve the common framework for sovereign debt relief for lower-income nations.

a2108.speaker: Local economists (Lesotho)
a2108.speech: Have warned that Lesotho should not be ecstatic with the IMF lifeline as the country "does not stand to benefit much".

a2108.speaker: Thabo Qhesi, independent economic analyst
a2108.speech: "There won't be too much impact to the likes of Lesotho, taking into account the debts that we already have which, are significantly high. So, getting new loans somehow has been discouraged. Even if it does happen, it won't be significant, it will be very minimal."

a2108.speaker: IMF Executive Board
a2108.speech: Announced on October 21 that it had on October 11 concluded the Review of Charges and the Surcharge Policy, which for the first time jointly covered charges, surcharges, and commitment fees; noted the review was part of a continuous effort to ensure the IMF's lending policies remain fit for purpose; noted it had reached a consensus on a comprehensive package of measures to "meaningfully reduce the cost of borrowing for members", preserve incentive mechanisms for prudent and temporary borrowing, and safeguard the strength of the IMF's balance sheet ; "Charges and surcharges are important elements of the IMF's cooperative lending and risk management framework. They provide incentives for prudent and temporary borrowing that help underpin the revolving nature of IMF resources and allow for the accumulation of reserves to mitigate financial risks. This supports the IMF's financial foundation, enabling it to play its role as a lender at the center of the global financial safety net."

a2130.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a2130.speech: "I think, as you know, that the response in Gaza, in the Gaza Strip, has been excessive," he said in an exchange with journalists at the White House on Thursday. ; "I am pushing very, very hard for humanitarian aid to reach Gaza."

a2130.speaker: Washington (US government)
a2130.speech: Warned Tel Aviv, a historic US ally, of the risk of a catastrophe in Rafah.

a2130.speaker: Local Health Ministry in Gaza controlled by Hamas (data)
a2130.speech: According to its data, Israel's offensive has so far caused more than 27,800 deaths and 61,317 injuries in the Gaza Strip.

a2130.speaker: Official Israeli figures
a2130.speech: According to the latest official Israeli figures, 1,140 people were killed in the 7 October Hamas attack on Israel, mostly civilians but also nearly 400 military personnel.

a2229.speaker: UNHCR (United Nations refugee agency)
a2229.speech: Warns that, because of post-electoral unrest, thousands of Mozambican refugees and civilians are facing immense risks, losing their livelihoods and depending on humanitarian aid; says that in Malawi it and the government have identified some 2,000 people who crossed the border last week, and that in neighbouring Eswatini another 1,000 people have arrived; specifies that among the new arrivals are refugees and asylum seekers of various nationalities who were living in Mozambique, and says it is worried about the escalation of displacement and its impact on affected populations.

a2229.speaker: Chansa Kapaya, UNHCR Regional Director for Southern Africa
a2229.speech: "We are deeply alarmed by the current situation in Mozambique, where the escalation of violence has forced thousands of people to flee. Refugees and civilians face immense risks, lose their livelihoods and depend on humanitarian aid. Although we are grateful for the generosity of Malawi and Eswatini, immediate support is crucial to deal with the worsening crisis and prevent further suffering."

a2229.speaker: People who fled Mozambique to Malawi
a2229.speech: Said they had escaped attacks and looting in their villages; many travelled long distances and crossed the Shire River on foot or in small boats to reach safety, among them pregnant women, elderly people and children who had had little to eat, according to UNHCR.

a2229.speaker: UNHCR (United Nations refugee agency)
a2229.speech: Maintains that it quickly provided tents, blankets and hygiene kits to help the most vulnerable, but that significant gaps remain in humanitarian aid: "Shelters are overcrowded, sanitation facilities are inadequate and access to food and drinking water is insufficient. More than 1,000 people share a single latrine at some sites, which considerably increases the risk of disease."

a2229.speaker: UNHCR (United Nations refugee agency)
a2229.speech: Says that in Eswatini many new arrivals report having lost their shops and businesses because of the violence, and that the Malindza refugee reception centre, initially designed for 250 people, is now overcrowded and houses more than 1,000 people; reports that it is working with local authorities and its partners to provide assistance, but that additional resources are urgently needed to support the response and prepare to receive more arrivals; and concludes in its note received by APA on Tuesday that the international community must urgently provide support to host countries and ensure that affected populations receive the aid they desperately need.

a2373.speaker: Ahmed Moalim Fiqi, Somali Foreign Minister
a2373.speech: Recently stated that the government would take decisive action against Abu Dhabi for what it perceives as a violation of Somalia's sovereignty.

a2373.speaker: Ali Bal'ad, State Minister of Foreign Affairs of Somalia
a2373.speech: Downplayed the incident, describing it as "not a big deal" and highlighting the UAE's longstanding support for Somalia.

a2449.speaker: Germaine Compaoré, Secretary General of the National Federation of Women Weavers of Burkina (FENATI-BF)
a2449.speech: Stressed that the 2024 activity programme had been rich in events, with successes and challenges to overcome: “In carrying out the 2024 activity programme, we went through rain and fair weather, through wind and tide, through ups and downs, we experienced successes and failures but we reached our destination.”

a2449.speaker: Germaine Compaoré, Secretary General of FENATI-BF
a2449.speech: Cited among the achievements the recognition of FENATI by the government and the institutions of Burkina Faso, participation in important decision-making bodies, collaboration with the Chamber of Trades and Crafts of Burkina Faso (CMA-BF) and the ministry in charge of Crafts and humanitarian actions, and mentioned that FENATI and some of its members had received honorary distinctions.

a2449.speaker: Germaine Compaoré, Secretary General of FENATI-BF
a2449.speech: Deplored the persisting challenges: “As for the difficulties, we can note the weak organisation of women weavers in certain regions, the use of imported thread in certain regions despite awareness-raising, the current lack of FILSAH coloured thread, the lack of training for the great mass of women weavers, the failure of certain women weavers to join organised weavers' structures, the flooding of markets with imported thread and woven wrappers, and consumers' failure to distinguish between Faso Dan Fani and imported woven wrappers despite awareness-raising.”

a2449.speaker: Members of FENATI-BF (general assembly)
a2449.speech: Decided to continue awareness-raising in the regions where imported thread is heavily used in order to encourage the use of Burkinabè thread, to mobilise funds for a vast mass-training campaign in sustainable artisanal dyeing techniques and standardised weaving in all regions, and to acquire land on which to build the federation's headquarters.

a2547.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM) (report)
a2547.speech: Reported that approximately 300 migrants attempting to cross the central Mediterranean were intercepted and returned to the Libyan coast between May 25 and May 31, 2025 ; documented that since the beginning of 2025 9,585 migrants have been returned to Libya, including 8,147 men, 960 women and 333 children, with 145 identified as unaccompanied minors or individuals requiring special assistance, and that as of May 31, 2025 at least 233 migrants had lost their lives at sea and another 225 were reported missing.

a2547.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a2547.speech: Consistently reiterates its stance that Libya cannot be considered a safe port for the disembarkation of migrants, and, while not involved in the interception operations themselves, provides vital humanitarian assistance upon the migrants' return while advocating for sustainable alternatives that uphold fundamental human rights.

a2551.speaker: Dr. Zohra Balsara, Health Office Director, USAID/Ghana
a2551.speech: Explained that the mobile clinic is equipped with an ultrasound machine and printer, an echocardiogram machine, two examination beds, three consulting rooms, air conditioners, a refrigerator for vaccines, a generator and power system ; said HopeXchange Medical Center in Kumasi will manage and operate the clinic and provide specialized medical screenings to communities in the Ashanti region and beyond ; expressed the hope that with the introduction of the mobile clinic, preventive, promotive and curative health services would be brought to the doorsteps of those who are unable to travel to Kumasi ; said the beauty of the HopeXchange model is that everyone has the right to the highest level of quality health care, embodying a true vision of equity ; said the HopeXchange Medical Center is a state-of-the-art health care facility managed by the Christian Health Authority of Ghana (CHAG) that serves four million people across Ghana ; said USAID has since 2013 provided $3.5 million to HopeXchange to, among other things, establish and equip its pathology laboratory for the Women's Cancer Center, support clinical and research programmes, and construct a maternal-child health center.

a2551.speaker: Dominic Osei Kofi, General Manager of HopeXchange Medical Center
a2551.speech: Expressed gratitude for the partnership of USAID/ASHA ; said HopeXchange has a dedicated outreach team of clinicians that conduct routine outreach to communities, and that from October 2023 to September 2024 the outreach team reached 12,517 people across 63 communities in the Ashanti and Bono East regions ; expressed optimism that the Mobile Clinic Van would enable the outreach team to significantly expand its community services and augment their outreach activities ; revealed that medical screening in rural and poor communities has been part of their services even before the start of the hospital and is now one of their core activities ; said about 20 persons identified with masses in their breasts during various outreaches received interventions ranging from ultrasound and CT scans and histopathological diagnosis to free surgery ; re-affirmed that the Mobile Clinic would allow the Outreach Team to reach underserved and remote communities nationwide, offering health education and medical screenings including specialized services, and provide essential free quality medical care to people who otherwise lack access, including children in need.

a2764.speaker: Ambassador Vrooman, U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a2764.speech: "Mozambique is a strategic partner of the United States. Our two countries continue to work together to strengthen ties in a wide range of areas, including issues related to security, but also development, investment, and infrastructure."

a2764.speaker: General Michael Langley, U.S. Marine Corps, commander of U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM)
a2764.speech: "I came here to discuss with Mozambique's security leaders how we find opportunities to address our shared challenges together. We discussed how we can achieve our common goals and expand our partnership. This includes integrating defence with diplomacy and development - the three Ds - to support our partners in Mozambique and build resilience to conflict and the myriad of challenges facing Mozambicans on a daily basis."

a2764.speaker: Ambassador Robert Scott, Deputy for Civil-Military Engagement, AFRICOM
a2764.speech: "We want the people of Mozambique to know, we are committed to our partnership and visits like today further expand the dialogue which inevitably produce dividends."

a2764.speaker: Maura Barry Boyle, USAID Senior Development Advisor
a2764.speech: "We also recognize the important work of those dedicated to addressing the challenges associated with marginalized groups."

a2764.speaker: U.S. Embassy in Mozambique (@USEmbassyMaputo, social media post)
a2764.speech: "General Michael Langley of the U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM) visited Mozambique from 15 to 16 August to hold meetings with President Nyusi and Admiral Mangrasse, reinforcing the crucial security partnership between the U.S. and Mozambique, and to discuss progress in the..."

a2825.speaker: Heads of State and Government of the East African Community (EAC) and the Southern African Development Community (SADC) (final communiqué)
a2825.speech: Expressed their condolences to the victims of the conflict and condemned the recent attacks on diplomatic missions in Kinshasa, underlining the urgency of a peaceful and lasting solution.

a2825.speaker: Heads of State and Government of the East African Community (EAC) and the Southern African Development Community (SADC) (summit decisions)
a2825.speech: Demanded an immediate ceasefire and the restoration of essential services to guarantee the delivery of humanitarian aid ; announced the merging of the Luanda and Nairobi peace processes into a single, strengthened framework intended to facilitate negotiations ; ordered that a meeting of the EAC and SADC chiefs of defence forces be held within five days to establish technical guidelines for securing Goma and the surrounding areas, and ordered the immediate reopening of Goma airport ; insisted on the need to resume direct negotiations with all parties, including the M23 rebel group which has occupied Goma ; called for the implementation of a plan to neutralise the FDLR and for modalities for the withdrawal of uninvited foreign armed forces from Congolese territory ; agreed to establish regular consultations, at least once a year, to examine questions of common interest and ensure follow-up of the commitments made ; thanked Tanzania for organising the meeting and called for swift and concerted action to restore stability in eastern DRC.

a2865.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of Benin
a2865.speech: Recalled, in his state-of-the-nation address delivered before the national representation in Porto-Novo, that 2015 confirms the good performance recorded over the past few years, performance resulting from reforms undertaken in all sectors of the national economy

a2865.speaker: Delegation of executive directors of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2865.speech: Acknowledged that the prudent policies of Benin's authorities have contributed to solid macroeconomic results, while noting that stronger, sustainable and more inclusive growth is essential to reduce poverty in the face of a more difficult environment, including the economic slowdown in neighbouring Nigeria

a2865.speaker: Djibril Salifou, General Manager of the Electricity Community of Benin (CEB)
a2865.speech: Said the start of work on the Adjarala mega project to secure electricity supply in reality marks the end of 30 years of famine under successive governments that spared no effort in seeking partners to finance it

a2865.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of Benin
a2865.speech: Made suggestions at the third India-Africa Forum Summit to boost economic relations between India and the African continent, saying the expertise acquired by India in various fields and the similarity of socio-economic realities with Africa predispose the continent to further develop cooperation matching the needs of African countries

a2880.speaker: Public health officials
a2880.speech: Warn that the loss of aid will lead to significant losses in livelihoods and lives.

a2880.speaker: Uganda's Health Ministry
a2880.speech: Has announced plans to close all dedicated HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis (TB) clinics due to the loss of USAID funding.

a2880.speaker: Brian Aliganyira, director of Ark Wellness Hub in Uganda
a2880.speech: The situation is described as "total panic" by local health leaders like Brian Aliganyira.

a2880.speaker: Flavia Kyomukama, National Forum of People Living with HIV/AIDS Networks Uganda
a2880.speech: Expressed shock at the sudden withdrawal of aid, calling it a betrayal that leaves communities reeling.

a2880.speaker: Experts
a2880.speech: Warn that these cuts have broader implications beyond Uganda's borders. They risk undermining vital programs like PEPFAR (President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief), which provides critical support globally in fighting against HIV/AIDS.

a2880.speaker: Analysts
a2880.speech: Indicate that such drastic reductions could lead to a systemic collapse of international aid frameworks if not addressed promptly by global leaders and donors alike.

a3020.speaker: Josephine Napwon, South Sudan Minister of Environment
a3020.speech: Highlighted the impact of the climate crisis in South Sudan, saying five years of catastrophic floods and dry spells have gutted livelihoods and left millions languishing in poverty; pointed out that her country is at the frontline of the climate disaster and stressed prolonged seasonal floods, excessive heatwaves and droughts that have killed livestock and led to crop failure. “The Climate Crisis has worsened since 2019, with severe flooding that led to internal displacement and loss of livelihoods” ; “This year, the same states are currently being flooded and over 1 million people are reported to have been affected and are in need of urgent humanitarian assistance” ; “Besides the flooding, droughts, excessive heat wave and haphazard rain patterns have resulted in crops failure thus impacting the livelihoods of our people especially in Eastern Equatoria and the northern parts of the country.”

a3020.speaker: Josephine Napwon, South Sudan Minister of Environment
a3020.speech: Noted that 60 percent of South Sudan’s population lives in extreme poverty and appealed for urgent lifesaving interventions: “Lifesaving interventions are needed urgently, hence the prospect of climate-induced displacement and climate ravages will become a new normal.”

a3020.speaker: 2023 INFORM Risk Index
a3020.speech: Ranks South Sudan as the second most vulnerable country globally to the impacts of natural hazards, including droughts and flooding, and among the top five countries most vulnerable to the impact of climate change.

a3020.speaker: Sheila Ngatia, UNDP Deputy Resident Representative
a3020.speech: Said the upcoming UN Climate Change conference presents a platform for frontline countries to be heard and believes that commitment to climate action is not only a responsibility but an opportunity to build a sustainable future for communities. “The upcoming COP29 presents an unprecedented opportunity to amplify our voices and to showcase our commitment to climate action” ; “We recognize that our commitment to climate action is not just a responsibility, it is an opportunity to build a sustainable future for our communities especially rural communities which are at the forefront of facing the brunt of the impact of climate change.”

a3020.speaker: Timo Olkkonen, EU Ambassador to South Sudan
a3020.speech: Underscored that international actors grappling with other crises facing the country should not overlook the climate issue, and stated that the time has come for the world to take action and mitigate the most important challenge facing mankind, otherwise the future generation will bear the brunt of today’s inaction. “With all the challenges facing South Sudan, it is not obvious that climate change would be at the forefront and as a priority for the country. Indeed globally, with all the crisis that are happening in the world, there is a danger that the issue of climate change will slip from the priority agenda” ; “And if this happens, then I am afraid the future generation will not look kindly at us if we indeed fail to use the opportunities still available to tackle the most important challenge facing humankind today.”

a3020.speaker: UN humanitarian agency
a3020.speech: According to the agency, since May 2024 floods have affected more than 1.4 million people across South Sudan, with livelihoods including farmlands and livestock wiped out, and hundreds of thousands forced from their homes.

a3111.speaker: Claudia Sheinbaum, Mexico’s President, and Justin Trudeau, Canada’s Prime Minister
a3111.speech: Announced a 30-day suspension on US tariffs after an agreement was reached with Trump; the two leaders agreed to send thousands of police to their borders with the US to fight drug trafficking and undocumented migration.

a3111.speaker: Democrat lawmakers
a3111.speech: Have questioned the legality of billionaire Elon Musk’s role in sweeping changes at key US federal government bodies, including Treasury and USAID.

a3111.speaker: Chinese government / Ministry of Finance office (statement)
a3111.speech: China said it would implement a 15% tariff on coal and liquefied natural gas products as well as a 10% tariff on crude oil, agricultural machinery and large-engine cars imported from the U.S., with the tariffs to take effect next Monday. ; “The US’s unilateral tariff increase seriously violates the rules of the World Trade Organization. It is not only unhelpful in solving its own problems, but also damages normal economic and trade cooperation between China and the US.”

a3111.speaker: China’s State Administration for Market Regulation
a3111.speech: Said Tuesday it is investigating Google on suspicion of violating antitrust laws.

a3166.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Namibian Minister of Health and Social Services
a3166.speech: says all U.S. funds allocated to local health programs, including HIV/AIDS initiatives, are accounted for: "Funds were advanced before the order took effect, meaning work will continue. We anticipate a positive review, and there is nothing suggesting Namibia is non-compliant with U.S. expectations. We are cautiously optimistic that operations will continue as usual."

a3166.speaker: Namibian Ministry of Health and Social Services
a3166.speech: assures that program rollouts remain unaffected for now.

a3166.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Namibian Minister of Health and Social Services
a3166.speech: reaffirms Namibia's accountability, stating that U.S. funds are managed by American agencies, not the Health Ministry: "The funds are not handled by the Ministry but by U.S.-established agencies. There is no indication of mismanagement on Namibia's part."

a3166.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Namibian Minister of Health and Social Services
a3166.speech: is confident Namibia's programs remain sustainable: "When we launched malaria, TB, and HIV/AIDS programs, they were government-led initiatives. They receive annual parliamentary appropriations, ensuring sustainability. Unlike some countries where donor funding covers 90% of costs, Namibia is not in that position."

a3475.speaker: Young Congolese woman met in transit in Nairobi (anonymous)
a3475.speech: Told me she could not get over it and that she regretted that the Rwandan troops had left Congo without teaching them discipline, good management and cleanliness.

a3475.speaker: Rwandan friend of the author, based in Lusaka
a3475.speech: Laughed and retorted: "You in Burundi, you are a 'no state'. I prefer," he told me, "a 'police state' like Rwanda to a 'no state' like Burundi."

a3475.speaker: Rwandan friend of the author, based in Lusaka
a3475.speech: Told me that we used to know banana republics, and that the world is now discovering an 'avocado' republic.

a3475.speaker: The author's taxi driver in Kigali (anonymous)
a3475.speech: As my taxi driver said, even Kagame's detractors cannot get over the progress recorded in only ten years.

a3475.speaker: A proponent of 'tropical Nazism' met in Malawi (anonymous)
a3475.speech: Told me in Malawi that the next genocide would be worse than the previous one.

a3475.speaker: General Dallaire, commander of the UN forces in Rwanda
a3475.speech: Had premonitory words: "if the RPF runs the country the way it waged the war, Rwanda will take off economically."

a3475.speaker: The NATO commander at the time (1994)
a3475.speech: Said that Kagame's victorious strategy should be taught in war colleges.

a3501.speaker: Patrick Youssef, ICRC's Head of Africa
a3501.speech: "We're custodians of the Geneva Conventions." ; described the ICRC's mission as a dual endeavour: providing life-saving assistance and advocating for the protection of civilians through the rigorous implementation of international humanitarian law; noted that the principles of neutrality, impartiality, and independence form the backbone of the ICRC's approach, enabling the organisation to access conflict zones where few others can operate. "Our work begins and ends with people - those displaced by violence, detainees, and communities caught in the crossfire of war," adding that the ICRC operates in over 20 African countries.

a3501.speaker: Patrick Youssef, ICRC's Head of Africa
a3501.speech: Highlighted the need for increased international attention to meet the extraordinary needs of crises in Africa daily; reiterated the importance of sustained international engagement, particularly in preventing the regional dimensions of African conflicts from spiralling further.

a3501.speaker: Patrick Youssef, ICRC's Head of Africa
a3501.speech: Spoke of the escalating violence in Sudan, particularly in Darfur, where millions are displaced; described how Sudan epitomises the multi-layered crises faced across Africa - ethnic violence, political instability, and mass displacement - and warned of the conflict's potential to destabilise neighbouring states; stressed the importance of global solidarity in tackling the root causes of these crises. "Sudan's crisis is a microcosm of what's happening across Africa - protracted, multifaceted conflicts with deep human consequences." He expressed concern about the long-term trajectory of the crisis, noting that the regional dimensions of Sudan's conflict could destabilise neighbouring countries like Chad and South Sudan.

a3501.speaker: Patrick Youssef, ICRC's Head of Africa
a3501.speech: On the financial front: "Our relationship with donors isn't just financial - it's a partnership that allows us to champion the protection of vulnerable populations and ensure adherence to humanitarian norms."

a3501.speaker: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a3501.speech: Maintains that donor contributions - particularly from the United States, which provides approximately 25 per cent of the organisation's funding through the State Department's Office of Population, Refugees, and Migration - must remain voluntary to preserve the organisation's independence and impartiality.

a3501.speaker: Patrick Youssef, ICRC's Head of Africa
a3501.speech: Emphasised that interventions in response to severe floods in West Africa, including Nigeria, are critical to addressing the growing impact of climate-related disasters on vulnerable communities already struggling with conflict.

a3501.speaker: Patrick Youssef, ICRC's Head of Africa
a3501.speech: In 2025, as Africa faces a year of escalating conflicts, his message was clear: the ICRC remains committed to its mission, but the international community must act with greater urgency to address the root causes of these crises.

a3593.speaker: U.S. Government / United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (announcement)
a3593.speech: announces that Mozambique was named a high priority country for the Global Water Strategy, which will guide USAID's work with the Government of the Republic of Mozambique over the next five years to strengthen the capacity of the water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) sector.

a3593.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a3593.speech: In 2022, WHO estimated that only 63 percent of the Mozambican population had access to basic water services, 38 percent of the population had access to basic sanitation facilities, and the national rate of open defecation was 29 percent.

a3593.speaker: Isobel Coleman, USAID Deputy Administrator
a3593.speech: highlighted on a recent visit to Nampula province that USAID is currently implementing WASH activities in close collaboration with the Mozambican government in Nampula, Zambezia, and Cabo Delgado; noted, "We believe that by working together, we can achieve our shared goal of providing safe water and sanitation for all Mozambicans."

a3727.speaker: British Colonial Office, Report by His Britannic Majesty’s government on the administration under mandate of Tanganyika Territory for the year 1924
a3727.speech: Described the Western limit of previously German territory as the median line of the Lake: “[…] Thence it follows the boundary of Rhodesia to the northern end of Lake Nyasa and continues along the centre line of Lake Nyasa to a point due west of the Rovuma River whence the boundary runs east and joins the Rovuma River, whose course it follows to the sea.”

a3727.speaker: Nyasaland annual general report for the year 1925 (Colonial Reports)
a3727.speech: Stated that: “This strip falls naturally into two divisions: (1) consisting of the western shore of Lake Nyasa, with the high tablelands separating it from the basin of the Luangwa river in Northern Rhodesia, and (2) the region lying between the watershed of the Zambesi river and Shire river on the west, and the Lakes Chiuta and Chilwa and the river Ruo, an affluent of the Shire, on the east, including the mountain systems of the Shire Highlands and Mlanje, and a small portion, also mountainous, of the south-eastern coast of Lake Nyasa.”

a3727.speaker: Great Britain (advice to the Council of the League of Nations, 1925)
a3727.speech: Advised the Council of the League of Nations that the boundary between Tanganyika and Nyasaland ran along the centre line of the Lake, submitting a map showing the boundary running through the middle of the lake.

a3727.speaker: British Government (1959 advice to the Government of Tanganyika)
a3727.speech: Advised the Government of Tanganyika that its legal advisers considered that no part of the Lake was within the boundaries of Tanganyika.

a3727.speaker: Minister for Lands and Mineral Resources, Tanganyika
a3727.speech: Stated in the Tanganyika Legislative Council in May 1959 that the borders of Tanganyika remained as they were demarcated by the 1890 Treaty.

a3727.speaker: Government of Tanganyika (declaration of 30 November 1961)
a3727.speech: Declared that it would honour bilateral treaties for two years and would then regard as terminated all treaties “which could not by the application of the rules of customary international law be regarded as otherwise surviving.”

a3727.speaker: Rashidi Kawawa, Prime Minister of Tanzania
a3727.speech: Stated in a speech to the National Assembly on 11 June 1962 that no part of Lake Nyasa lay within the borders of Tanzania, and further stated that the earlier statement of 30 November 1961 did not affect this issue.

a3727.speaker: Organisation of African Unity (OAU) resolution, 21 June 1964
a3727.speech: Passed a resolution providing that “[…] all member states pledge themselves to respect the frontiers existing on their achievement of national independence.”

a3727.speaker: Government of Tanzania (official notification, January 1967)
a3727.speech: Officially notified Malawi it considered the boundary to run through the middle of the Lake.

a3727.speaker: Government of Malawi (reply of 24 January 1967)
a3727.speech: Informed Tanzania it would consider the issue and a further reply would follow.

a3727.speaker: Tanzanian President (letter of 31 May 1967 to his Malawian counterpart)
a3727.speech: Advised that Tanzania rejected the shoreline boundary.

a3727.speaker: President of Malawi
a3727.speech: Publicly rejected Tanzania’s claim as having no justification.

a3727.speaker: Authorities
a3727.speech: State that about 1.5 million Malawians and 600,000 Tanzanians depend on the Lake for food, transportation and other daily needs.

a3727.speaker: Local environmentalists
a3727.speech: Fear that drilling in the Lake will damage eco-tourism and the marine environment affecting Tanzania’s northern fishing region.

a3727.speaker: Reports (Nation on Sunday, ‘The Malawi-Tanzania Border Dispute, Voices from the frontiers’)
a3727.speech: Cite lakeshore communities’ greater concern as to the threat of oil exploration than the rights of the respective parties.

a3727.speaker: The World Bank and the Food and Agriculture Organisation
a3727.speech: As at 1995, recognised three categories of fisherman on Lake Malawi: artisanal, semi-commercial and commercial.

a3727.speaker: Economic Recovery Plan (ERP) introduced by Joyce Banda’s Cabinet in 2012
a3727.speech: Prioritises mining, along with commercial agriculture, tourism, and energy, as “quick wins.”

a3814.speaker: Marine Le Pen, president of the National Rally (RN) parliamentary group
a3814.speech: regrets that Donald Trump’s decision to “pause” the payment of aid to Kyiv “does not leave it a reasonable amount of time to adjust” ; “I consider that the brutality of this decision is reprehensible,” she judged, denouncing a “cruel decision for Ukrainian soldiers,” speaking to Le Figaro on Tuesday ; “No one can force the United States to maintain its support if that country no longer wishes to do so,” while considering it “highly open to criticism not to leave Ukraine a reasonable amount of time to adjust.”

a3814.speaker: Marine Le Pen, president of the RN parliamentary group
a3814.speech: in her speech to the National Assembly on Monday, regretted “Western intransigence towards Russia” ; repeating the words she had already chosen at the podium on Monday evening, again said she was opposed to “the chimerical idea” of a “European defence” and to “sending French combat troops onto Ukrainian soil.”

a3814.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a3814.speech: announced a “pause” in United States military aid to Ukraine on 3 March.

a3814.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a3814.speech: is willing to “open” the discussion on nuclear deterrence with his European partners; the head of state raised the hypothesis of sending European troops to Ukraine at the London summit on Sunday, in the event of the signing of a truce between Ukraine and Russia.

a3819.speaker: UNAIDS (report published Thursday 10 July in Johannesburg)
a3819.speech: says the fight against AIDS will suffer from the halt to American aid, and fears that more than 20 years of progress may be called into question ; according to UNAIDS, around 31.6 million people were receiving antiretroviral treatment in 2024 and deaths linked to the virus have fallen by more than half compared with 2010, to 630,000 per year.

a3819.speaker: UNAIDS
a3819.speech: has done its calculations: with the end of the American emergency plan for AIDS relief (PEPFAR), more than six million new infections and 4.2 million additional deaths would be recorded in only four years, and the pandemic would return to levels comparable to those of the early 2000s ; according to the UNAIDS report, more than 60% of the women’s associations fighting AIDS that were contacted have already lost funding or suspended services, and in Nigeria the number of people on preventive prophylactic treatment fell by 85% over the first months of 2025 ; in 25 of the 60 low- and middle-income countries studied by UNAIDS, governments have been able to offset part of the shortfall through local financing.

a3819.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS
a3819.speech: “We are proud of our results but worried about this sudden interruption, which is erasing the progress that has been made” ; “This is not just a lack of money, it is a time bomb.”

a3819.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS
a3819.speech: argues for national responses, financed directly by the countries concerned; she calls for debt relief and for a reform of the international financial institutions, with the objective of creating fiscal space to allow developing countries to take charge of their own response.

a3819.speaker: South African government (official figures)
a3819.speech: According to government figures, in 2024 South Africa has around 8 million people living with HIV, or 12.7% of the population.

a4017.speaker: Colin Deiner, head of the Western Cape’s disaster management services
a4017.speech: Said they were on high alert on Tuesday evening: “We have not received any information on major damage other than the Eskom substation in Witzenberg, which has since been restored. We will commence with a damage assessment as soon as this storm warning has passed.”

a4017.speaker: Charlotte Powell, City of Cape Town Disaster Risk Management spokesperson
a4017.speech: Said they received reports of flooded roadways in Du Noon, Somerset West, Gordon’s Bay, Strand and Muizenberg ; said approximately 50 homes were flooded in informal settlements in Masiphumelele and that the South African Social Security Agency (Sassa) was activated to provide humanitarian assistance.

a4017.speaker: Bertha Peters-Scheepers, Johannesburg Roads Agency (JRA) spokesperson
a4017.speech: Said Hendrik Potgieter Road was closed near Raceworx KTM, after part of the road collapsed ; said a bridge on Kilburn Street and Wilgerood Road in Roodepoort also collapsed, and traffic was being diverted.

a4017.speaker: David Tembe, City of Johannesburg Public Safety MMC
a4017.speech: Said the storm on Friday, 9 December was the worst of the recent downpours ; added that Emergency Management Services (EMS) officials were inundated with reports from all parts of the city.

a4017.speaker: News24 (report)
a4017.speech: Reported on Monday that City of Johannesburg Public Safety MMC David Tembe said the storm on Friday, 9 December was the worst of the recent downpours.

a4017.speaker: Eskom
a4017.speech: Said this request — Johannesburg Mayor Mpho Phalatse’s urgent request for a three-day load shedding exemption — was under review.

a4084.speaker: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, owner of X and head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a4084.speech: Pledged to "fix" X's fact-checking tool and claimed that his social media platform's "community notes" feature was being "gamed" by governments and traditional media; did not provide evidence of manipulation of X's community notes system; also did not substantiate a claim that widely reported polling by the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology was "Zelensky-controlled" and "not credible".

a4084.speaker: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, owner of X (post on X)
a4084.speech: "If Zelensky was actually loved by the people of Ukraine, he would hold an election. He knows he would lose in a landslide, despite having seized control of ALL Ukrainian media, so he cancelled the election," while sharing the unsubstantiated claim that US intelligence agencies estimate Zelensky's approval to be just 4% ; "In reality, he is despised by the people of Ukraine, which is why he has refused to hold an election." ; "I challenge Zelensky to hold an election and refute this. He will not."

a4084.speaker: Lucas Graves, journalism professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison
a4084.speech: Described Musk's comments as "extremely concerning". "As is often the case with this kind of rhetoric, the accusations are a guide to what we have to look out for from the accuser - a world where private platforms like X can be systematically gamed to favour the political interests and alliances of their owners." ; "A well-designed community notes system can be a useful check on misinformation. But that requires transparent rules that make it easy for users to surface reliable information, and that can't be tweaked at the whim of one person."

a4084.speaker: John Wihbey, associate professor of media innovation and technology at Northeastern University
a4084.speech: Said an inescapable feature of crowdsourced fact-checking models is that a platform's owner or management may not like the results. "Overall, I think community notes is a good approach, but it should be blended with other tools. X is now relying on it too much, and it is ironic that leadership is now complaining that it isn't working well."

a4084.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4084.speech: On Wednesday, accused Zelensky of being a "dictator" after the Ukrainian leader rejected his claims that Kyiv was to blame for the war and raised concerns about being sidelined in Washington's negotiations with Moscow; also claimed that Zelensky was "very low" in the polls in his country, echoing an earlier claim that he had an approval rating of just 4%.

a4084.speaker: Kyiv International Institute of Sociology (opinion poll)
a4084.speech: In an opinion poll carried out on Wednesday, 57% of respondents said they trusted Zelensky, up five points from December. The institute's polling also shows the Ukrainian leader's popularity has waned as the war has gone on, dropping from 90% in March 2022 to 64% in February 2024.

a4084.speaker: Center for Countering Digital Hate (analysis)
a4084.speech: An analysis published by the nonprofit found that nearly three-quarters of false or misleading posts about the 2024 US elections that were studied did not display accurate notes correcting the record.

a4084.speaker: Gordon Pennycook, professor of psychology at Cornell University
a4084.speech: "I think there's a strong chance that X/Twitter becomes a propaganda arm for Musk/Trump - and, in fact, it's already happening." ; "I think Musk wants to reform community notes because he doesn't like being corrected, as is typical for authoritarian oligarchs."

a4205.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4205.speech: Mocked Lesotho last month as a country “nobody has ever heard of”, and announced the 50 percent tariff as part of a sweeping set of “reciprocal tariffs” laid out on Thursday.

a4205.speaker: The Trump administration
a4205.speech: Claims Lesotho imposes a 99 percent tariff on US goods.

a4205.speaker: Oxford Economics
a4205.speech: According to Oxford Economics, in 2024 Lesotho’s exports to the US totalled $237m, accounting for more than 10 percent of its GDP.

a4205.speaker: The Lesotho government
a4205.speech: Did not comment immediately on the trade tariffs.

a4205.speaker: Lesotho’s foreign minister (to Reuters news agency, last month)
a4205.speech: Told Reuters the country, which has one of the highest HIV/AIDS infection rates in the world, was feeling the impact of the aid cuts as the health sector had been reliant on them.

a4297.speaker: Alemayehu Geda (PhD), macroeconomist and university professor
a4297.speech: Says the new federal budget is very expansionary, claiming that the budget did not factor in the adverse impact of the pandemic on the economy ; views the target for tax revenues as ambitious, predicting that domestic tax revenues collection could shrink by 18pc this coming fiscal year: “This is due to a decline in external trade and economic activity in the country.”

a4297.speaker: Alemayehu Geda (PhD), macroeconomist and university professor
a4297.speech: Argues this kind of ambitious projection will lead to the request of a supplementary budget, therefore increasing the budget deficit ; “In an effort to fill the budget gap, the government will opt for inflationary financing.”

a4297.speaker: Alemayehu Geda (PhD), macroeconomist and university professor
a4297.speech: On the government’s plan to lower headline inflation to 9.8pc and reach 8.5pc growth: “This is unachievable with the current uncertain economy and political instability”; estimates economic growth will contract by 11pc under the assumption the virus is contained by December ; recommended: “The government should come back to earth and reprioritise its expenses and focus on funneling resources to the mitigation of the virus as fast as possible.”

a4297.speaker: Abiy Ahmed (PhD), Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a4297.speech: Said during the session when the budget bill was legislated that the tax collection performance for the entire year would not exceed 200 billion Br, which is only 80pc of the targeted value.

a4297.speaker: Eyob Tekalign (PhD), State Minister for Finance
a4297.speech: Begs to differ with Alemayehu’s opinion, arguing that the tax revenue projection is attainable: “It’s achievable, although it requires a lot of work and coordination,” he told Fortune. “We’re working extensively on the administration side at the Ministry of Revenues and at Customs, both in infrastructural and customer centric projects.” ; “We aren’t pessimistic about the economy.”

a4297.speaker: Eyob Tekalign (PhD), State Minister for Finance
a4297.speech: “We expect to generate close to 50 billion Br from the sale of T-bills by the coming fiscal year.”

a4297.speaker: Eyob Tekalign (PhD), State Minister for Finance
a4297.speech: “It’s a very critical year. Potential expenditures are focused on the production sectors; the economy needs stimulus and the economic reform we are following will thread in coordination.” ; “In the worst scenario where the government can’t meet the ballooning tax collection target, we’ll have to cut our expenditures.”

a4300.speaker: Ussene Isse, Minister of Health of Mozambique
a4300.speech: Announced that Mozambique had stocks of medicine sufficient for the next nine months, but admitted “challenges” in getting the drugs to patients ; “Before the announcements from the United States [of suspension of support] we had stock for nine months in the country, and with the relief we are calm (…) in terms of the quantity of medicine. But now the challenge is to get the medicine to the patient’s mouth. This is fundamental, and we all have to work together.”

a4300.speaker: Ussene Isse, Minister of Health of Mozambique
a4300.speech: “I came to the conclusion that we have the conditions in the country to solve the main health problems, because I found a production line for medicines here that responds to the profile of diseases in our country. These factories will be able to export to neighbouring countries, because they are of high quality.” (after visiting two pharmaceutical factories in Maputo province, which he challenged to produce medicines for the National Health System with a view to reducing external dependence)

a4300.speaker: Official USAID data web page (data captured by Lusa on February 4)
a4300.speech: Shows that among members of the Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP), Mozambique received the most USAID aid in 2023, totalling US$664.122 million (€639.70 million), followed by Angola with US$71.320 million, Brazil with US$68.985 million and Timor-Leste with US$43.688 million; 2023 is the most recent fiscal year for which there is complete information.

a4300.speaker: Association of United and Solidary Health Professionals of Mozambique (APSUSM)
a4300.speech: Demands that the government provide medicines to hospitals, which in some cases have to be purchased by patients; acquire hospital beds and address the “lack of food”; equip ambulances with emergency materials and non-disposable personal protective equipment, the lack of which is “forcing employees to buy out of their own pockets”.

a4300.speaker: Citizen Observatory for Health (OCS)
a4300.speech: Asked the Mozambican government in June 2024 for clarification about the alleged lack of “essential” medicines in public hospitals, despite pointing out that there is “sufficient stock” for patients to be treated.

a4300.speaker: Mozambican government
a4300.speech: Confirmed in the same month that it spends eight billion meticais (€116 million) annually on the acquisition of medicines.

a4300.speaker: Inocêncio Impissa, spokesman for the Mozambican government and Minister of State Administration and Public Service
a4300.speech: Said on February 7 that the suspension of US funding also has implications for the acquisition and distribution of medicines, and highlighted the importance of support to maintain strategic and priority health programs in Mozambique, such as the fight against HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis, among other diseases.

a4468.speaker: José Manuel Albares, Spanish Minister of Foreign Affairs
a4468.speech: “We all have to implement an arms embargo. There can be no sale of arms to Israel”, calling for a review of the national list of individual sanctions that each country and the EU have ; recalled that Spain has been applying individual sanctions for some time and, without ruling out “any” additional sanctions, encouraged the other countries to work together to be more effective and to apply specific measures.

a4468.speaker: José Manuel Albares, Spanish Minister of Foreign Affairs
